title: Editor crash (use-after-free): AnimationPlayerEditor::get_state calls get_path_to() on a freed player when switching scene tabs
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f] (Windows editor, field crash)
- The unguarded code is still present in current master (editor/animation/animation_player_editor_plugin.cpp:909)


### System information

Windows, Godot v4.7.stable.official — Forward+ (crash is platform-independent by mechanism; analyzed against the official Windows binary)

### Issue description

The editor hard-crashes (access violation / signal 11) during the per-scene state save
that runs on a scene-tab switch. Symbolizing the official 4.7 win64 binary at the crash
offsets gives this chain (innermost first):

  Node::get_path_to                       scene/main/node.cpp (the common_parent walk, ~line 2366)
  AnimationPlayerEditor::get_state        d["player"] = ...get_edited_scene()->get_path_to(player)
  AnimationPlayerEditorPlugin::get_state
  EditorData::save_edited_scene_state / get_editor_plugin_states
  EditorNode::_set_current_scene_nocheck
  EditorNode::load_scene
  FileSystemDock (double-click on a scene file)

i.e. `AnimationPlayerEditor::player` pointed at a freed AnimationPlayer, and get_state
walked its dangling parent chain.

Why the pointer can dangle — `player` is a raw pointer with two invalidation holes:

1. `AnimationPlayerEditor::set_state()` assigns `player` but does NOT update
   `original_node` (only `edit()` sets it). The cleanup path
   `_node_removed(p_node)` only clears `player` when `original_node == p_node`,
   so a set_state-restored player whose `original_node` is stale is invisible to
   the cleanup: when that node later leaves the tree and is freed, `player` keeps
   pointing at it. In normal in-editor tab switches this is masked because the
   restored selection re-runs `edit()` via `_edit_current()` right afterwards —
   but `EditorNode::reload_instances_with_path_in_edited_scenes()` (the
   reimport/reload machinery) ends with `editor_data.restore_edited_scene_state()`
   (→ set_state) with NO `_edit_current()` repair after it.

2. Nodes freed while OUT of the tree never fire `SceneTree::node_removed` at all
   (`_node_removed` is connected to that signal), e.g. subtrees replaced/detached
   by the scene-reload machinery, or a non-current tab being closed
   (`EditorData::remove_scene` memdeletes an out-of-tree root).

`get_state()` then dereferences `player` behind only a null check:

    if (EditorNode::get_singleton()->get_edited_scene() && is_visible_in_tree() && player) {
        d["player"] = EditorNode::get_singleton()->get_edited_scene()->get_path_to(player);

Field sequence that produced the crash (project folder was being written to
externally — a cloud-synced folder, which drives the resources_reimported →
scene-reload machinery repeatedly while multiple tabs are open):

1. Open a scene with an AnimationPlayer, use the Animation panel. (Works fine.)
2. Close that tab, edit another scene (one with no AnimationPlayer, so nothing
   re-points the panel).
3. Double-click the first scene in the FileSystem dock to reopen it.
4. On the tab switch, save_edited_scene_state → AnimationPlayerEditor::get_state →
   get_path_to(freed player) → crash. Never crashes on the FIRST open — the first
   engagement goes through edit(), which sets both pointers consistently.

Suggested fix: track the player by ObjectID and resolve it before use (the same
file already uses this pattern for `cached_root_node_id`), or at minimum set
`original_node` in `set_state()` and validate `player` via ObjectDB in
`get_state()`/`_ensure_dummy_player()`.

Possibly related: #106362, #78735.

Original crash log (win64, official build):

```
CrashHandlerException: Program crashed with signal 11
Engine version: Godot Engine v4.7.stable.official (5b4e0cb0fd279832bbdd69fed5354d4e5ad26f88)
[6] 7ff6a178741f (main+245741f)   <- Node::get_path_to
[7] 7ff6a096252e (main+163252e)   <- AnimationPlayerEditor::get_state
[8] 7ff6a54b09c3 (main+61809c3)   <- AnimationPlayerEditorPlugin::get_state
[9] 7ff6a08cadf0 (main+159adf0)   <- editor_data.cpp (get_editor_plugin_states)
[10] 7ff6a08d48ac (main+15a48ac)  <- editor_data.cpp (save_edited_scene_state)
[11] 7ff6a0935833 (main+1605833)  <- EditorNode::_set_current_scene_nocheck
[13] 7ff6a093eec6 (main+160eec6)  <- EditorNode::load_scene
[14] 7ff6a0b3e53a (main+180e53a)  <- FileSystemDock::_navigate_to_path / _select_file
[17] 7ff6a1bb43db (main+28843db)  <- ItemList double-click
```
(full log available on request; symbol names recovered by disassembling the
official binary around each offset and reading the referenced error-macro strings)

### Steps to reproduce

No deterministic minimal repro — the arming step needs the scene-reload machinery to
run set_state without a following _edit_current (external file modification while the
editor is open, multiple tabs, Animation panel engaged), or an out-of-tree free of the
tracked player. The use-after-free itself is visible by code inspection at
animation_player_editor_plugin.cpp: set_state() (does not set original_node),
_node_removed() (guard: original_node == p_node), get_state() (unguarded deref).


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A (editor lifecycle bug, no project-specific asset required; happens in a large
multi-scene project whose files change on disk while the editor is open)
